newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania shares pick up ahead of H1 bank results.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania shares pick up ahead of H1 bank results.

text.p: Rising expectations regarding key banking sector results injected new life into Lithuania's struggling bourse on Tuesday, with Hermis Bank leading the way.
Central market volume was just over one million litas, well up from Monday's 247,000 litas.
Hermis Bank and Vilniaus Bank both gained, pulling up the official index by 9.59 points to 899.14.
"Investors are expecting good six-month results from both banks," said one dealer.
But nervousness remains about other six-month results and the wider group A index shed 4.68 points to 1,871.16.

Hermis Bank was the most active stock, rising almost five percent to 195 litas in central market trade of 498,000 litas. It also turned over 333,000 litas in block trades in the price range of 187 litas to 195 litas.
Dealers have said for some time that the bank, the country's second largest private bank, looked undervalued and it was expected to gain ahead of its first half results.
The bank also just completed a 23 million litas share capital issue and a road show which have raised its profile with foreign investors.
Rival Vilniaus Bank, the country's largest private bank, rose to 237 litas from 235 litas in trade of 108,000 litas.
